notes: Uses a cleaner per-series exemplar storage lookup, releases chunks and the mmap-ready count correctly, and has good tests including cutoff expiry and a unit test for zero and negative timestamps. Same variadic optional-parameter hack, plus the same unrelated go.mod/go.sum bump and go.work deletion.

This is a valid alternative: it checks the circular exemplar storage live by labels to decide whether to keep a series, releases chunks, the appender and mmap-ready state, and its tests are thorough. However, it threads an optional retain func through variadic params, does not protect exemplars before they are committed, and adds unrelated go.mod/go.sum bumps plus a go.work deletion.

Retention works by asking the exemplar storage which series have exemplars at or after the cutoff. Weaknesses: it rebuilds a map of every such series on each GC, uses a variadic parameter as an optional-argument hack, and shares one buffer inside the closure. Unrelated edits bump go.mod/go.sum and delete go.work.

It works and passes, but it precomputes a label-keyed set of series from exemplar storage once per GC, which is a snapshot that can miss exemplars committed during GC and uses a shared buffer in a closure. It also uses variadic optional params and includes unrelated go.mod/go.sum/go.work changes; its checkpoint helper in the tests is weak.

Tracks the newest exemplar timestamp on memSeries and sets it on commit, WAL replay and snapshot load; both GC paths keep the series and release chunks, the appender and the mmap-ready count. Two small weaknesses: unlike the reference, which marks the series at append time, it leaves a small race window before commit, and the new head_test is inserted under an existing test's doc comment.

It closely mirrors the reference: a per-series max exemplar timestamp plus a has-exemplar flag, set on commit, WAL replay and snapshot restore, with chunk, appender and mmap-ready release and a clean internal signature change. Tests are strong, but it records the timestamp at commit rather than append, and the new test is inserted so that it steals an existing test's doc comment.

The approach is nearly identical to C1, but the non-variadic change to stripeSeries.gc likely breaks existing test call sites, so the hidden tests and package suite fail. It also leaves series.app set in the regular gc path and marks exemplars during replay even when exemplar storage is disabled.

Tracking the max exemplar timestamp per memSeries is close to the reference. But ordinary gc does not clear the stale appender, the non-variadic stripeSeries.gc signature change breaks compatibility, all hidden tests fail and the package suite fails.
